The prohibition fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern prohibition-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as prohibition coded rather than literal no-smoking-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🚭 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate prohibition-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'prohibition 🚭' prohibition-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'no-pulse pulse 🚭' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'prohibition coded 🚭' list thread. The prohibition fill cue is what makes the emoji feel prohibition coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'prohibition coded no-smoking moment.'

What separates 🚭 from the rest of the shape family is the prohibition register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'prohibition coded no-smoking,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🚭 travels especially well on partner prohibition-marker markers, prohibition-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with prohibition energy.
